The claimant is in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability of the Insurer and also seeking for enhancement.

2. The Tribunal has exonerated the Insurer on the ground that the driver of the maxi cab did not possess the requisite endorsement to drive the vehicle and he only possessed the licence to drive the light motor vehicle.

3. In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED - (2017) 14 SCC 663, this finding cannot be sustained and it will have to be held that the Insurer would be liable to pay the compensation.

In arriving at the said sums, the Tribunal has accepted the disability assessed by the Doctor at 40%, but, however, has determined the notional income at Rs.5,000/-.

Since there is no evidence to establish the actual income of the claimant, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2011, would be Rs.6,500/-.
Since the claimant has suffered 40% disability and was aged 49 years as on the date of the accident, 25% future prospects requires to be added, which makes his income to be Rs.8,125/-.

6. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.5,07,000/- (Rs.8,125/- X 12 X 13 X 40%)
towards loss of future earnings.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.90,000/- towards pain and sufferings and Rs.30,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant has suffered 40% disability and was hospitalised for 49 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards pain and sufferings and Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities.
8. A sum of Rs.5,48,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses and a sum of Rs.35,000/- awarded towards future medical expenses, being based on documentary evidence, are affirmed.

9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.38,000/- towards food, nourishment, attendant charges,
etc.
Having regard to the fact that the claimant was hospitalised 49 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges.
10. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as five months.
In my view, since the claimants was hospitalised for 49 days, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as six months.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.39,000/- (Rs.6,500/- X 6 months) towards loss of income during laid up period.
11. Thus, in modification of the award of the Tribunal, the claimant would be entitled to the following sums as compensation:
